title.zh: 卷三百四十三 列傳第一百〇二 元絳 許將 鄧潤甫 林希 蔣之奇 陸佃 吳居厚 溫益
title.en: Volume 343 Biographies 102: Yuan Jiang, Xu Jiang, Deng Runfu, Lin Xi, Jiang Zhiqi, Lu Tian, Wu Juhou, Wen Yi
title.raw: 卷三百四十三 列傳第一百〇二 元絳 許將 鄧潤甫 林希 蔣之奇 陸佃 吳居厚 溫益 Volume 343 Biographies 102: Yuan Jiang, Xu Jiang, Deng Runfu, Lin Xi, Jiang Zhiqi, Lu Tian, Wu Juhou, Wen Yi

sentences.zh: 元絳，字厚之，其先臨川危氏。

translations.literal: Yuan Jiang, styled Houzhi; his ancestors were the Wei clan of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jiang, styled Houzhi, came from the Wei clan of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 唐末，曾祖仔倡聚眾保鄉里，進據信州，為楊氏所敗，奔杭州，易姓曰元。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tang, his great-great-grandfather Zai led a band to protect the village, advanced to seize Xinzhou, was defeated by the Yang clan, fled to Hangzhou, and changed the surname to Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tang dynasty, his great-great-grandfather Zai raised a band to defend their home district, advanced to occupy Xinzhou, was defeated by the Yang clan, fled to Hangzhou, and changed the family name to Yuan.

sentences.zh: 祖德昭，仕吳越至丞相，遂為錢塘人。

translations.literal: His grandfather Dezhao served Wu-Yue up to Chancellor, and thus became a man of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Dezhao served the Wu-Yue kingdom, rising to Chancellor, and the family thus became natives of Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 絳生而敏悟，五歲能作詩，九歲謁荊南太守，試以三題，上諸朝，貧不能行。

translations.literal: Jiang was born sharp and perceptive; at five he could compose poetry; at nine he visited the Jingnan prefect and was tested on three topics, which he submitted to the court, but he was too poor to travel.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang was born quick and perceptive. At five he could write poetry; at nine he called on the prefect of Jingnan, was tested on three topics, and sent the results to court—but he was too poor to make the journey himself.

sentences.zh: 長，舉進士，以廷試誤賦韻，得學究出身。

translations.literal: When grown he passed the jinshi examination, but in the palace examination he miscalled the rhyme in the fu and received the rank of xuejiu.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he passed the jinshi examination, but in the palace examination he used the wrong rhyme in his fu and received only the lower rank of research graduate.

sentences.zh: 再舉登第，調江寧推官，攝上元令。

translations.literal: On a second attempt he passed and was appointed judicial assistant at Jiangning, acting as magistrate of Shangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On his second attempt he passed the examination and was appointed judicial assistant at Jiangning, serving concurrently as acting magistrate of Shangyuan.

sentences.zh: 民有號王豹子者，豪占人田，略男女為僕妾，有欲告者，則殺以滅口。

translations.literal: Among the people was one styled Wang the Leopard who forcibly seized others' fields, abducted men and women as servants and concubines, and killed those who wished to accuse him to silence them.
translations.idiomatic: Among the people was a man known as Wang the Leopard who seized others' land by force, kidnapped men and women as servants and concubines, and murdered anyone who tried to report him.

sentences.zh: 絳捕置於法。

translations.literal: Jiang captured him and punished him according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang arrested him and punished him according to law.

sentences.zh: 甲與乙被酒相毆擊，甲歸臥，夜為盜斷足。

translations.literal: A and B, both drunk, fought each other; A returned to bed, and in the night a burglar cut off his feet.
translations.idiomatic: A and B, both drunk, fought each other. A went home to sleep, and in the night a burglar cut off his feet.

sentences.zh: 妻稱乙，告里長，執乙詣縣，而甲已死。

translations.literal: The wife accused B; she reported to the village head, who seized B and brought him to the county, but A was already dead.
translations.idiomatic: The wife accused B. She reported to the village head, who seized B and brought him to the county seat—but A was already dead.

sentences.zh: 絳敕其妻曰：「歸治而夫喪，乙已伏矣。」

translations.literal: Jiang ordered the wife: "Go prepare your husband's funeral—B has already confessed."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang told the wife, "Go home and prepare your husband's funeral. B has already confessed."

sentences.zh: 陰使信謹吏跡其後，望一僧迎笑，切切私語。

translations.literal: He secretly sent a trustworthy and careful clerk to follow her; watching, he saw a monk come forward smiling, and they whispered together intently.
translations.idiomatic: Secretly he sent a reliable, careful clerk to follow her. The clerk saw a monk come forward with a smile, and the two whispered together at length.

sentences.zh: 絳命取僧繫廡下，詰妻奸狀，即吐實。

translations.literal: Jiang ordered the monk seized and bound beneath the corridor, questioned the wife about the adultery, and she immediately confessed the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang had the monk seized and bound under the corridor, questioned the wife about the affair, and she immediately confessed.

sentences.zh: 人問其故，絳曰：「吾見妻哭不哀，且與傷者共席而襦無血污，是以知之。」

translations.literal: When people asked the reason, Jiang said: "I saw the wife weep without grief, and that she shared a mat with the wounded man yet her jacket had no bloodstains—therefore I knew."
translations.idiomatic: When people asked how he knew, Jiang said, "I saw that the wife's weeping was not truly mournful, and that though she shared a mat with the wounded man, her jacket had no blood on it—that is how I knew."

sentences.zh: 安撫使范仲淹表其材，知永新縣。

translations.literal: The pacification commissioner Fan Zhongyan memorialized his talent, and he was appointed magistrate of Yongxin County.
translations.idiomatic: The pacification commissioner Fan Zhongyan recommended his ability, and he was appointed magistrate of Yongxin County.

sentences.zh: 豪子龍聿誘少年周整飲博，以技勝之，計其貲折取上腴田，立券。

translations.literal: A powerful man's son, Long Yu, enticed the young man Zhou Zheng to drink and gamble; winning by skill, he calculated his assets and seized fine fields in exchange, drawing up a contract.
translations.idiomatic: The son of a powerful family, Long Yu, lured the young man Zhou Zheng into drinking and gambling. Beating him by skill, he calculated Zhou's assets and took his best fields in settlement, drawing up a contract.

sentences.zh: 久而整母始知之，訟於縣，縣索券為證，則母手印存，弗受。

translations.literal: After a long time Zhou Zheng's mother learned of it and sued at the county; the county demanded the contract as proof, but the mother's handprint was on it, and they would not accept the case.
translations.idiomatic: Only after a long time did Zhou Zheng's mother learn of it and sue at the county. The county demanded the contract as evidence, but since the mother's handprint was on it, they refused to accept her claim.

sentences.zh: 又訟於州，於使者，擊登聞鼓，皆不得直。

translations.literal: She sued again at the prefecture, at the commissioner, and beat the drum to appeal to the throne, but nowhere could she obtain justice.
translations.idiomatic: She appealed again at the prefecture, before the commissioner, and by beating the drum at the imperial audience hall—but nowhere could she obtain justice.

sentences.zh: 絳至，母又來訴，絳視券，呼謂聿曰：「券年月居印上，是必得周母他牘尾印，而撰偽券續之耳。」

translations.literal: When Jiang arrived, the mother came to sue again; Jiang looked at the contract and called to Yu: "The date on the contract comes above the seal—this must mean you obtained the tail of some other document with Zhou's mother's seal and forged the contract by continuing it."
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang arrived, the mother came to sue again. Jiang examined the contract and called to Yu, "The date on this contract sits above the seal—you must have taken the end of some other document bearing Zhou's mother's seal and forged this contract by continuing from it."

sentences.zh: 聿駭謝，即日歸整田。

translations.literal: Yu was alarmed and apologized, and that same day returned Zheng's fields.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was alarmed and apologized, returning Zhou Zheng's fields that same day.

sentences.zh: 知通州海門縣。

translations.literal: He became magistrate of Haimen County in Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Haimen County in Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 淮民多盜販鹽，制置使建言，滿二十斤者皆坐徒。

translations.literal: Huai River people often stole and trafficked in salt; the fiscal commissioner proposed that anyone with twenty jin or more should be sentenced to penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: People along the Huai River often smuggled salt. The fiscal commissioner proposed that anyone caught with twenty jin or more should be sentenced to penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 絳曰：「海濱之人，恃鹽以為命，非群販比也。」

translations.literal: Jiang said: "People of the seacoast rely on salt for their livelihood—they cannot be compared with organized smuggling bands."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang said, "People of the seacoast depend on salt for their livelihood—they cannot be lumped together with professional smuggling gangs."

sentences.zh: 笞而縱之。

translations.literal: He flogged them and released them.
translations.idiomatic: He had them flogged and released them.

sentences.zh: 擢江西轉運判官、知台州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to transport vice-commissioner of Jiangxi and magistrate of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to transport vice-commissioner of Jiangxi and appointed magistrate of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 州大水冒城，民廬蕩析。

translations.literal: The prefecture suffered great floodwaters that washed over the city walls; people's houses were swept away and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: A great flood washed over the city walls of the prefecture, and people's homes were swept away and destroyed.

sentences.zh: 絳出庫錢，即其處作室數千區，命人自占，與期三歲償費，流移者皆復業。

translations.literal: Jiang took money from the treasury and on the spot built several thousand dwellings, letting people claim them for themselves, with a three-year period to repay the cost; displaced persons all returned to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang drew on treasury funds to build several thousand dwellings on the spot, letting people choose their own, with three years to repay the cost. All the displaced returned to their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 又甓其城，因門為牐，以禦湍漲，後人守其法。

translations.literal: He also faced the city walls with brick and made sluice gates at the gates to resist surging floods; later men kept to his method.
translations.idiomatic: He also faced the city walls with brick and built sluice gates at the city gates to hold back surging waters. Later officials kept to his methods.

sentences.zh: 入為度支判官。

translations.literal: He entered [the capital] as vice-director of the Revenue Department.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as vice-director of the Revenue Department.

sentences.zh: 儂智高叛嶺南，宿軍邕州 而歲漕不足。

translations.literal: Nong Zhigao rebelled in Lingnan; troops were stationed at Yongzhou yet annual transport was insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: When Nong Zhigao rebelled in Lingnan, troops were stationed at Yongzhou, but annual grain transport fell short.

sentences.zh: 絳以直集賢院為廣東轉運使，建瀕江水砦數十，以待逋寇；

translations.literal: Jiang, holding a straight post at the Hall of Assembled Worthies, was made Guangdong transport commissioner; he built dozens of forts along the riverside to await fleeing bandits;
translations.idiomatic: Jiang, serving as a direct appointee at the Hall of Assembled Worthies, was made Guangdong transport commissioner. He built dozens of riverside forts to intercept fleeing bandits;

sentences.zh: 繕治十五城，樓堞械器皆備，軍食有餘。

translations.literal: repaired fifteen cities so that parapets and weapons were all ready, and military provisions were ample.
translations.idiomatic: repaired fifteen cities so that towers, parapets, and weapons were all in readiness, and military provisions were more than sufficient.

sentences.zh: 以功遷工部郎中，歷兩浙、河北轉運使，召拜鹽鐵副使，擢天章閣待制、知福州，進龍圖閣直學士，徙廣、越、荊南，為翰林學士、知開封府，拜三司使、參知政事。

translations.literal: For his merit he was moved to director in the Ministry of Works, successively transport commissioner in the two Zhe and Hebei, summoned and appointed vice-commissioner of Salt and Iron, promoted to academician awaiting orders at the Hall of Heavenly Patterns and magistrate of Fuzhou, advanced to direct academician at the Dragon Diagram Hall, transferred to Guang, Yue, and Jingnan, made Hanlin academician and magistrate of Kaifeng, appointed commissioner of the three fiscal departments and Vice Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was promoted to director in the Ministry of Works, then served successively as transport commissioner in the Two Zhes and Hebei. He was summoned and appointed vice-commissioner of Salt and Iron, promoted to academician awaiting orders at the Hall of Heavenly Patterns and magistrate of Fuzhou, advanced to direct academician at the Dragon Diagram Hall, transferred through Guang, Yue, and Jingnan, made Hanlin academician and magistrate of Kaifeng, and finally appointed commissioner of the three fiscal departments and Vice Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 數請老，神宗命其子耆寧校書崇文院，慰留之。

translations.literal: He repeatedly requested retirement; Shenzong had his son Qining made collator at the Academy of Scholarly Glory to comfort him and keep him in office.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly asked to retire. Shenzong appointed his son Qining as collator at the Academy of Scholarly Glory to comfort him and keep him in office.

sentences.zh: 會太學虞蕃訟博士受賄，事連耆寧，當下獄。

translations.literal: Then the Imperial University student Yu Fan sued the doctor for taking bribes; the matter implicated Qining, who should have been thrown into prison.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Imperial University student Yu Fan sued a lecturer for taking bribes, and the case implicated Qining, who should have been thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 絳請上還職祿，而容耆寧即訊於外，從之。

translations.literal: Jiang requested to return his salary and post, while Qining might be questioned outside [the prison]; [the emperor] consented.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang asked to return his salary and office, requesting that Qining be allowed to be questioned outside prison instead. The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是御史至第薄責絳，絳一不自辨，罷知亳州。

translations.literal: Thereupon censors came to his residence to audit and reprimand Jiang; Jiang did not defend himself at all and was dismissed to be magistrate of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon censors came to his residence to audit and reprimand him. Jiang offered no defense at all and was dismissed to serve as magistrate of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 入辭，帝謂曰：「朕知卿，一歲即召矣。

translations.literal: Upon entering to take leave, the emperor said: "I know you—you will be summoned within a year.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to take leave, the emperor said, "I know you well—you will be recalled within a year.

sentences.zh: 卿意欲陳訴乎？」

translations.literal: Do you wish to lodge an appeal?"
translations.idiomatic: Do you wish to lodge an appeal?"

sentences.zh: 絳謝罪，願得潁，即以為潁州。

translations.literal: Jiang apologized and asked to be assigned to Ying; he was immediately made [magistrate of] Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang apologized and asked to be assigned to Ying. He was immediately appointed magistrate of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，加資政殿學士、知青州，過都，留提舉中太一宮，力疾入謁，曰：「臣疾憊子弱，儻一旦不幸死，則遺骸不得近先人丘墓。」

translations.literal: The next year he was given the additional title of academician of the Hall of Asset Administration and assigned to Qingzhou; passing through the capital, he was retained to direct the Palace of Grand Unity of the Central [Heaven] and, though ill, entered to pay audience, saying: "I am ill and worry my sons are weak; if I should suddenly die, my remains would not be able to lie near my ancestors' tombs."
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was given the additional title of academician of the Hall of Asset Administration and assigned to Qingzhou. Passing through the capital, he was retained to direct the Palace of Grand Unity of the Central Heaven. Though ill, he forced himself to attend audience and said, "I am ill, and I worry my sons are weak. If I should die suddenly, my remains would not lie near my ancestors' tombs."

sentences.zh: 帝惻然曰：「朕為卿辦襄，雖百子何以加。」

translations.literal: The emperor was moved and said: "I will arrange your funeral for you—how could a hundred sons add more?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved and said, "I will arrange your funeral for you—what could a hundred sons add to that?"

sentences.zh: 詔毋多拜，乘輿行幸勿扈從。

translations.literal: He decreed that Jiang need not bow repeatedly and need not accompany imperial processions.
translations.idiomatic: He decreed that Jiang need not perform repeated bows and need not accompany the imperial carriage on processions.

sentences.zh: 又明年，以太子少保致仕。

translations.literal: The next year he retired as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he retired with the title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 絳所至有威名，而無特操，少儀矩。

translations.literal: Wherever Jiang went he had a stern reputation, yet he had no exceptional integrity and little regard for propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Jiang served he earned a reputation for sternness, yet he lacked exceptional moral fiber and paid little heed to propriety.

sentences.zh: 仕已顯，猶謂遲晚。

translations.literal: Even after attaining prominence, he still felt his advancement had come late.
translations.idiomatic: Even after he had risen to high office, he still felt his advancement had come too late.

sentences.zh: 在翰林，諂事王安石及其子弟，時論鄙之。

translations.literal: In the Hanlin, he flattered Wang Anshi and his sons; contemporary opinion despised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: While in the Hanlin Academy he fawned on Wang Anshi and his sons, and public opinion despised him for it.

sentences.zh: 然工於文辭，為流輩推許。

translations.literal: Yet he was skilled in literary composition and was praised by his peers.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was skilled in literary composition and was well regarded by his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 景靈宮作神御十一殿，夜傳詔草《上梁文》，遲明，上之。

translations.literal: When the Jingling Palace built eleven spirit halls for imperial portraits, at night he was ordered to draft the "Raising the Beam" inscription; by dawn he submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingling Palace built eleven spirit halls for imperial portraits, he was ordered at night to draft the Raising-the-Beam inscription. By dawn he had submitted it.

sentences.zh: 雖在中書，而蕃夷書詔，猶多出其手。

translations.literal: Even though he was in the Secretariat, foreign and frontier documents and edicts still mostly came from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Even after he entered the Secretariat, documents and edicts concerning foreign peoples and frontier affairs still came mostly from his hand.

sentences.zh: 既得謝，帝眷眷命之曰：「卿可營居京師，朕當資幣金，且便耆寧仕進。」

translations.literal: Having received leave to retire, the emperor fondly charged him: "You may establish a residence in the capital; I will supply funds, and Qining may advance in office as well."
translations.idiomatic: Having granted him retirement, the emperor spoke to him with deep affection: "You may establish a residence in the capital. I will supply the funds, and this will also ease Qining's path to office."

sentences.zh: 絳曰：「臣有田廬在吳，乞歸鬻之，即築室都城，得望屬車之塵，幸矣。

translations.literal: Jiang said: "I have fields and a house in Wu; I beg to return and sell them, then build a dwelling in the capital—merely to glimpse the dust of Your Majesty's carriage would be fortune enough.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang said, "I have fields and a house in Wu. I beg to return and sell them, then build a dwelling in the capital. Merely to catch sight of the dust of Your Majesty's carriage would be fortune enough.

sentences.zh: 敢冀賜邪。」

translations.literal: How dare I hope for a gift?"
translations.idiomatic: How dare I hope for a gift from Your Majesty?"

sentences.zh: 既行，追齎白金千兩，敕以蚤還。

translations.literal: After he departed, [the emperor] sent after him a thousand taels of white silver and ordered him to return early.
translations.idiomatic: After he departed, the emperor sent after him a thousand taels of white silver and ordered him to return soon.

sentences.zh: 絳至吳逾歲，以老病奏，恐不能奉詔。

translations.literal: Jiang reached Wu and after more than a year memorialized on account of old age and illness, fearing he could not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang reached Wu, and after more than a year he memorialized on account of old age and illness, saying he feared he could not obey the edict.

sentences.zh: 三年而薨，年七十六。

translations.literal: Three years later he died, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he died, at the age of seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少師，諡曰「章簡」。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, with posthumous title "Zhangjian" (Plain and Simple).
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given the title of Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous name Zhangjian (Plain and Simple).

sentences.zh: 許將，字沖元，福州閩人。

translations.literal: Xu Jiang, styled Chongyuan, a native of Min in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jiang, styled Chongyuan, was a native of Min in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 舉進士第一。

translations.literal: He placed first in the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He placed first in the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 歐陽修讀其賦，謂曰：「君辭氣似沂公，未可量也。」

translations.literal: Ouyang Xiu read his fu and said: "Your literary spirit resembles Duke Yi—your measure cannot yet be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu read his fu and said, "Your literary spirit resembles Duke Yi of Wang. Your future cannot yet be measured."

sentences.zh: 簽書昭慶軍判官，代還，當試館職，辭曰：「起家為官，本代耕爾，願以守選餘日，讀所未見書。」

translations.literal: As signing secretary and judge of the Zhaoging Army, when his term ended and he should have taken the examination for a post in the academies, he declined: "Taking office from the beginning is merely to stand in for farming; I wish to use the remaining days while awaiting selection to read books I have not yet seen."
translations.idiomatic: As signing secretary and judge of the Zhaoging Army, when his term ended and he was due to take the examination for an academy post, he declined: "Taking office from the start is merely to stand in for farming. I wish to use the remaining days while awaiting appointment to read books I have not yet seen."

sentences.zh: 宰相善其志，以通判明州。

translations.literal: The chief councilor approved his purpose and appointed him vice-prefect of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The chief councilor approved his purpose and appointed him vice-prefect of Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 神宗召對，除集賢校理、同知禮院，編修中書條例。

translations.literal: Shenzong summoned him for audience and appointed him collator at the Hall of Assembled Worthies and associate director of the Board of Rites, to compile regulations of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong summoned him for audience and appointed him collator at the Hall of Assembled Worthies and associate director of the Board of Rites, with responsibility for compiling regulations of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 自太常丞當轉博士，超改右正言；

translations.literal: From assistant director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices he should have been promoted to doctor, but was specially changed to right remonstrator;
translations.idiomatic: From assistant director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices he should normally have been promoted to doctor, but was specially advanced to right remonstrator;

sentences.zh: 明日，直舍人院；

translations.literal: the next day, duty in the Academy of Scholars;
translations.idiomatic: the next day, assigned to duty in the Academy of Scholars;

sentences.zh: 又明日，判流內銓，皆神宗特命，舉朝榮之。

translations.literal: the next day again, judge of the Board of the Flow Within—all special appointments by Shenzong; the whole court regarded it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: and the day after that, judge of the Board of the Flow Within—all special appointments by Shenzong. The whole court regarded it as an honor.

sentences.zh: 初，選人調擬，先南曹，次考功，綜核無法，吏得緣文為奸，選者又不得訴長吏。

translations.literal: Initially when selecting officials for assignment, [the process went] first to the Southern Office, then to the Merit Office; review had no fixed law, clerks could manipulate documents for fraud, and candidates could not appeal to senior officials.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, when selecting officials for appointment, cases went first to the Southern Office and then to the Merit Office. Review had no fixed standards, clerks could manipulate documents for fraud, and candidates could not appeal to senior officials.

sentences.zh: 將奏罷南曹，辟公舍 以待來訴者，士無留難。

translations.literal: Jiang memorialized to abolish the Southern Office and opened public offices to await those coming to appeal; officers had no delays or difficulties.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang memorialized to abolish the Southern Office and opened public offices to receive those coming to appeal. Candidates encountered no delays or obstruction.

sentences.zh: 進知制誥，特敕不試而命之。

translations.literal: He was promoted to draft edicts, specially ordered without examination.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to drafter of edicts, specially appointed by imperial order without examination.

sentences.zh: 契丹以兵二十萬壓代州境，遣使請代地，歲聘之使不敢行，以命將。

translations.literal: The Khitan pressed the border of Daizhou with two hundred thousand troops and sent envoys demanding land; the annual tribute envoy did not dare go, and the mission was given to Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan pressed the border of Daizhou with two hundred thousand troops and sent envoys demanding territory. The envoy for the annual tribute mission did not dare go, and the assignment was given to Jiang.

sentences.zh: 將入對曰：「臣備位侍從， 朝廷大議不容不知。

translations.literal: Jiang entered and replied: "I occupy a place among attendants—the great deliberations of court surely cannot be unknown to me.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang entered and replied, "I hold a place among the emperor's attendants—the great deliberations of court surely cannot be unknown to me.

sentences.zh: 萬一北人言及代州事，不有以折之，則傷國體。」

translations.literal: If by any chance the northerners speak of Daizhou, without something to refute them the dignity of the state would be injured."
translations.idiomatic: If by any chance the northerners raise the matter of Daizhou and I have nothing with which to refute them, the dignity of the state will be injured."

sentences.zh: 遂命將詣樞密院閱文書。

translations.literal: He was then ordered to go to the Bureau of Military Affairs to examine documents.
translations.idiomatic: He was then ordered to go to the Bureau of Military Affairs to review the relevant documents.

sentences.zh: 及至北境，居人跨屋棟聚觀，曰：「看南朝狀元。」

translations.literal: When he reached the northern border, residents straddled roof beams to gather and watch, saying: "Look at the Song dynasty zhuangyuan."
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the northern border, residents straddled roof beams to gather and watch, saying, "Look—the zhuangyuan of the Southern Court."

sentences.zh: 及肄射，將先破的。

translations.literal: When they practiced archery, Jiang was first to hit the target.
translations.idiomatic: When they practiced archery, Jiang was the first to hit the target.

sentences.zh: 契丹使蕭禧館客，禧果以代州為問，將隨問隨答。

translations.literal: The Khitan envoy Xiao Xi received the guests as host; Xi indeed raised Daizhou as a question, and Jiang answered each question as it came.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan envoy Xiao Xi served as host to the guests. Xi indeed raised the question of Daizhou, and Jiang answered each point as it came.

sentences.zh: 禧又曰：「界渠未定，顧和好體重，吾且往大國分畫矣。」

translations.literal: Xi also said: "The boundary ditch is not yet fixed; considering the gravity of friendly relations, I shall go to your great state to demarcate."
translations.idiomatic: Xi also said, "The boundary ditch is not yet fixed. Considering the gravity of friendly relations, I shall go to your great state to demarcate it."

sentences.zh: 將曰：「此事，申飭邊臣豈不可，何以使為？」

translations.literal: Jiang said: "This matter—would it not suffice to instruct the frontier officials sternly? Why need an envoy?"
translations.idiomatic: Jiang said, "On this matter, would it not suffice to instruct the frontier officials sternly? Why need an envoy?"

sentences.zh: 禧慚不能對。

translations.literal: Xi was shamed and could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was shamed and could not reply.

sentences.zh: 歸報，神宗善之，以將知審官西院、直學士院、判尚書兵部。

translations.literal: Reporting on return, Shenzong approved; Jiang was made director of the Western Court for Review of Appointments, duty in the Academy of Worthies, and judge of the Ministry of War in the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On his return and report, Shenzong approved. Jiang was made director of the Western Court for Review of Appointments, assigned to duty in the Academy of Worthies, and judge of the Ministry of War in the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時河北保甲、陝西河東弓箭社、閩楚槍仗手雖有名籍，其多少與年月不均，以致閱按無法，將一切整攝之。

translations.literal: At the time the Hebei militia, Shaanxi-Hedong crossbow societies, and Min-Chu pike-and-staff men, though they had registers, their numbers and dates were uneven, so inspection had no method; Jiang standardized them all.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Hebei militia, the Shaanxi-Hedong crossbow societies, and the Min-Chu pike-and-staff corps all had registers, but their numbers and dates were inconsistent, making inspection impossible. Jiang standardized them all.

sentences.zh: 進翰林學士、權知開封府，為同進所忌。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Hanlin academician and acting magistrate of Kaifeng, envied by fellow entrants.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin academician and acting magistrate of Kaifeng, arousing the envy of fellow entrants.

sentences.zh: 會治太學虞蕃訟，釋諸生無罪者，蔡確、舒亶因陷之，逮其父子入御史府，逾月得解，黜知蘄州。

translations.literal: When the case of Yu Fan at the Imperial University was handled, he released the students who were innocent; Cai Que and Shu Dan used this to frame him, seized him and his father and son into the Censorate, and after more than a month they obtained release; he was demoted to magistrate of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the case of Yu Fan at the Imperial University was handled, he released the students who were innocent. Cai Que and Shu Dan used this to frame him, seized him and his father and son and sent them to the Censorate. After more than a month they obtained release, but he was demoted to magistrate of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，以龍圖閣待制起知秦州，改揚州，又改鄆州。

translations.literal: The next year he was recalled as academician awaiting orders at the Dragon Diagram Hall to be magistrate of Qinzhou, changed to Yangzhou, then changed again to Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was recalled as academician awaiting orders at the Dragon Diagram Hall and appointed magistrate of Qinzhou, then transferred to Yangzhou, and then to Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 上元張燈，吏籍為盜者繫獄，將曰：「是絕其自新之路也。」

translations.literal: On the Lantern Festival lamps were hung; clerks registered thieves and imprisoned them; Jiang said: "This cuts off their path to reform."
translations.idiomatic: On the Lantern Festival, when lamps were hung, clerks registered known thieves and imprisoned them. Jiang said, "This cuts off their path to reform."

sentences.zh: 悉縱遣之，自是民無一人犯法，三圄皆空。

translations.literal: He released them all; from then on not a single person broke the law, and all three prisons were empty.
translations.idiomatic: He released them all. From then on not a single person broke the law, and all three prisons stood empty.

sentences.zh: 父老歎曰：「自王沂公後五十六年，始再見獄空耳。」

translations.literal: The elders sighed: "Since Duke Yi of Wang, after fifty-six years we see empty prisons once again."
translations.idiomatic: The elders sighed and said, "Since Duke Yi of Wang, fifty-six years have passed before we see empty prisons again."

sentences.zh: 鄆俗士子喜聚肆以謗官政，將雖弗禁，其俗自息。

translations.literal: The custom in Yan was for scholar-gentry to gather in shops to slander official policy; Jiang though he did not forbid it, the custom died down of itself.
translations.idiomatic: The custom in Yan was for scholar-gentry to gather in taverns to slander official policy. Though Jiang did not forbid it, the custom died down of its own accord.

sentences.zh: 召為兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 上疏言：「兵措於形勢之內，最彰而易知；

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: "Troops deployed within visible formations are most conspicuous and easy to discern;
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial saying, "Troops deployed within visible formations are most conspicuous and easy to discern;

sentences.zh: 隱於權用之表，最微而難能。

translations.literal: troops hidden beneath the table of strategic employment are most subtle and hard to master.
translations.idiomatic: troops hidden beneath the surface of strategic deployment are most subtle and hardest to master.

sentences.zh: 此天下之至機也。

translations.literal: This is the utmost pivot of the empire.
translations.idiomatic: This is the supreme pivot of the empire.

sentences.zh: 是以治兵有制，名雖不同，從而橫之，方而圓之，使萬眾猶一人；

translations.literal: Therefore in governing troops there is regulation: though names differ, following them one arrays them horizontally, squaring them round, making ten thousand men like one man;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in governing troops there is regulation: though the names differ, by following them one arrays them horizontally, squares them and rounds them, making ten thousand men move as one;

sentences.zh: 車馬有數，用雖不同，合而分之，散而斂之，取四方猶跬步；

translations.literal: for chariots and horses there are numbers: though uses differ, combining them one divides them, dispersing one gathers them, taking the four directions as a short step;
translations.idiomatic: for chariots and horses there are fixed numbers: though their uses differ, by combining them one divides them, by dispersing one gathers them, and reaching the four directions is like a single step;

sentences.zh: 製器有度，工雖不同，左而右之，近而遠之，運眾算猶掌握。

translations.literal: for making implements there are standards: though crafts differ, left and right, near and far, moving multitudinous reckonings is like [holding them in] the palm.
translations.idiomatic: for making implements there are standards: though the crafts differ, by moving left and right, near and far, one handles multitudinous calculations as if they were in the palm of one's hand.

sentences.zh: 非天下之至神，孰能與此？」

translations.literal: Unless one possessed the utmost spirit of the empire, who could achieve this?
translations.idiomatic: Unless one possessed the supreme spirit of the empire, who could achieve this?

sentences.zh: 又條奏八事，以為「兵之事有三：曰禁兵，曰廂兵，曰民兵。

translations.literal: He also submitted eight items in sequence, holding that "matters of troops have three: forbidden troops, garrison troops, and militia.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted eight items in sequence, holding that "matters of troops fall into three categories: forbidden troops, garrison troops, and militia.

sentences.zh: 馬之事有三：曰養馬，曰市馬，曰牧馬。

translations.literal: Matters of horses have three: raising horses, purchasing horses, and herding horses.
translations.idiomatic: Matters of horses fall into three: raising horses, purchasing horses, and herding horses.

sentences.zh: 兵器之事有二：曰繕作，曰給用。」

translations.literal: Matters of weapons have two: repair and manufacture, and supply and use."
translations.idiomatic: Matters of weapons fall into two: repair and manufacture, and supply and use."

sentences.zh: 及西方用兵，神宗遣近侍問兵馬之數，將立具上之；

translations.literal: When war was waged in the west, Shenzong sent a close attendant to ask the numbers of troops and horses; Jiang immediately compiled and submitted them;
translations.idiomatic: When war was waged in the west, Shenzong sent a close attendant to ask the numbers of troops and horses. Jiang immediately compiled and submitted a full report;

sentences.zh: 明日，訪樞臣，不能對也。

translations.literal: The next day, [the attendant] visited the chief ministers, but they could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he consulted the chief ministers, but they could not answer.

sentences.zh: 以龍圖閣直學士知成都府。

translations.literal: As direct academician at the Dragon Diagram Hall he was made magistrate of Chengdu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Chengdu Prefecture with the title of direct academician at the Dragon Diagram Hall.

sentences.zh: 元祐三年，再為翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanyou he again became Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Yuanyou era, he again became a Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 四年，拜尚書右丞。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 將自以在先朝為侍從，每討熙、豐舊章以聞。

translations.literal: Jiang himself, having served as attendant in the previous reign, each time investigated the old regulations of the Xining and Yuanfeng eras and reported them.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang himself, having served as an attendant in the previous reign, regularly investigated the old regulations of the Xining and Yuanfeng eras and reported them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 中旨用王文郁、姚兕領軍，執政復議用張利一、張守約。

translations.literal: An imperial order appointed Wang Wenyu and Yao Si to lead the army; the chief administrators reconsidered and proposed Zhang Liyi and Zhang Shouyue.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial order appointed Wang Wenyu and Yao Si to lead the army, but the chief administrators reconsidered and proposed Zhang Liyi and Zhang Shouyue instead.

sentences.zh: 將始與執政同議，復密疏利一不可用。

translations.literal: Jiang at first agreed with the chief administrators, then secretly memorialized that Liyi was unsuitable.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang at first agreed with the chief administrators, then secretly memorialized that Zhang Liyi was unsuitable.

sentences.zh: 言者論其窺伺主意，炫直賣友。

translations.literal: Critics argued that he was probing the emperor's intent and displaying uprightness while betraying his friends.
translations.idiomatic: Critics charged that he was probing the emperor's intent and parading his integrity while betraying his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 罷為資政殿學士、知定州，移揚州，又移大名府。

translations.literal: He was dismissed to be academician of the Hall of Asset Administration and magistrate of Dingzhou, transferred to Yangzhou, then again to Daming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed to serve as academician of the Hall of Asset Administration and magistrate of Dingzhou, then transferred to Yangzhou, and then to Daming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會黃河東、北二議未決，將曰：「度今之利，謂宜因梁村之口以行東，因內黃之口以行北，而盡閉諸口，以絕大名諸州之患。

translations.literal: When the two proposals for the eastern and northern courses of the Yellow River were undecided, Jiang said: "Considering present advantage, it is best to follow the Liangcun outlet for the eastern course and the Neihuang outlet for the northern course, and close all other outlets to eliminate the calamity to Daming and the other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When the two proposals for the eastern and northern courses of the Yellow River remained undecided, Jiang said, "Considering present advantage, the best course is to follow the Liangcun outlet for the eastern flow and the Neihuang outlet for the northern flow, and close all other outlets to eliminate the threat to Daming and the surrounding prefectures.

sentences.zh: 俟水大至，觀故道足以受之，則內黃之口可塞；

translations.literal: Wait until the water rises greatly; if the old channel can receive it, then the Neihuang outlet may be blocked;
translations.idiomatic: Wait until the flood peaks. If the old channel can carry it, then the Neihuang outlet may be blocked;

sentences.zh: 不足以受之，則梁村之口可以止；

translations.literal: if it cannot receive it, then the Liangcun outlet may be stopped;
translations.idiomatic: if it cannot, then the Liangcun outlet may be stopped;

sentences.zh: 兩不能相奪，則各因其自流以待之。」

translations.literal: if neither can prevail over the other, then let each follow its own flow and wait."
translations.idiomatic: if neither can prevail, then let each follow its own course and wait."

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，入為吏部尚書，上疏乞依元豐詔，定北郊夏至親祀。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaosheng he entered [the capital] as Minister of Personnel and submitted a memorial requesting that according to the Yuanfeng edict, the northern suburban sacrifice at the summer solstice be personally performed.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shaosheng era, he entered the capital as Minister of Personnel and submitted a memorial requesting that, in accordance with the Yuanfeng edict, the emperor personally perform the northern suburban sacrifice at the summer solstice.

sentences.zh: 拜尚書左丞、中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 章惇為相，與蔡卞同肆羅織，貶謫元祐諸臣，奏發司馬光墓。

translations.literal: When Zhang Dun became chief councilor, he and Cai Bian together fabricated charges, demoted and exiled the Yuanyou officials, and memorialized to exhume Sima Guang's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Dun became chief councilor, he and Cai Bian together fabricated charges, demoted and exiled the Yuanyou officials, and memorialized to exhume Sima Guang's tomb.

sentences.zh: 哲宗以問將，對曰：「發人之墓，非盛德事。」

translations.literal: Zhezong asked Jiang; he replied: "Exhuming a person's tomb is not a deed of great virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Zhezong asked Jiang about this. He replied, "Exhuming a person's tomb is not the act of a ruler of great virtue."

sentences.zh: 方黨禍作，或舉漢、唐誅戮故事，帝復問將，對曰：「二代固有之，但祖宗以來未之有，本朝治道所以遠過漢、唐者，以未嘗輒戮大臣也。」

translations.literal: When the factional disaster arose, some cited the precedents of executions in Han and Tang; the emperor again asked Jiang, who replied: "The two dynasties indeed had such cases, but since our ancestors there has been none. The reason our dynasty's governance far surpasses Han and Tang is that we have never casually executed great ministers."
translations.idiomatic: When the factional purge began, some cited the precedents of executions in the Han and Tang dynasties. The emperor again asked Jiang, who replied, "Those dynasties indeed had such cases, but since our founding ancestors there has been none. The reason our dynasty's governance far surpasses Han and Tang is that we have never casually executed great ministers."

sentences.zh: 哲宗皆納之。

translations.literal: Zhezong accepted all of this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhezong accepted all of this.

sentences.zh: 將嘗議正夏人罪，以涇原近夏而地廣，謀帥尤難，乞用章楶，楶果有功。

translations.literal: Jiang once discussed punishing the Tangut people; because Jingyuan was near Xia and the territory was broad, finding a commander was especially difficult; he requested Zhang Jie, and Jie indeed achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang once discussed punishing the Tangut people. Because Jingyuan bordered Xia and the territory was vast, finding a commander was especially difficult. He recommended Zhang Jie, who indeed achieved success.

sentences.zh: 崇寧元年，進門下侍郎，累官金紫光祿大夫，撫定鄯、廓州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongning he was promoted to Vice Director of the Chancellery, accumulated the rank of Grandee of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, and pacified Shan and Kuo prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Chongning era, he was promoted to Vice Director of the Chancellery, rose to the rank of Grandee of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, and pacified Shan and Kuo prefectures.

sentences.zh: 邊臣欲舉師渡河，朝議難之。

translations.literal: Frontier officials wished to raise an army and cross the river; court deliberation found it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier officials wished to raise an army and cross the river, but the court deliberation found it difficult to approve.

sentences.zh: 將獨謂：「外國不可以爽信，而兵機有不可失，既已戒期，願遂從之。」

translations.literal: Jiang alone said: "Foreign states cannot be treated with broken faith, and military opportunity cannot be missed; since the date has already been set, I wish we would proceed."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang alone said, "Foreign states cannot be treated with broken faith, and military opportunity cannot be missed. Since the date has already been set, I wish we would proceed."

sentences.zh: 未幾，捷書至，將以復河、湟功轉特進，凡居政地十年。

translations.literal: Before long, victory reports arrived; Jiang was promoted to special advance for recovering the He and Huang regions; in all he held power for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, victory reports arrived. Jiang was promoted to special advance for recovering the He and Huang regions. In all he held power for ten years.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞朱諤取將舊謝章表，析文句以為謗，且謂：「將左顧右視，見利則回，幡然改圖，初無定論。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Zhu E took Jiang's old memorials of thanks and parsed the sentences as slander, saying: "Jiang looks left and right, turns when he sees profit, suddenly changes course, and from the first has no fixed judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Zhu E took Jiang's old memorials of thanks and parsed the sentences as slander, charging, "Jiang looks left and right, turns when he sees profit, suddenly changes course, and from the first has had no fixed judgment.

sentences.zh: 元祐間嘗為丞轄，則盡更元豐之所守。

translations.literal: During Yuanyou he once served as vice-director, then completely changed what Yuanfeng had upheld.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanyou era he once served as vice-director, then completely overturned what the Yuanfeng era had upheld.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初復秉鈞軸，則陰匿元祐之所為。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaosheng he again held the helm, then secretly concealed what Yuanyou had done.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shaosheng era he again held the helm of state, then secretly concealed what the Yuanyou era had done.

sentences.zh: 逮至建中，尚此冒居，則紹聖之所為已皆非矣。

translations.literal: By the time of Jianzhong, still shamelessly holding office, what Shaosheng had done was already all wrong.
translations.idiomatic: By the time of the Jianzhong era, still shamelessly holding office, what the Shaosheng era had done was already all wrong.

sentences.zh: 強顏今日，亦復偷安，則建中之所為亦隨改焉。」

translations.literal: Putting on a bold face today, again seeking ease, what Jianzhong has done will also change accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Putting on a bold face today and again seeking ease, what the Jianzhong era has done will also change accordingly.

sentences.zh: 遂以資政殿大學士知河南府。

translations.literal: He was then made grand academician of the Hall of Asset Administration and magistrate of Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made grand academician of the Hall of Asset Administration and magistrate of Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 言者不已，降資政殿學士、知潁昌府，移大名，加觀文殿學士、奉國軍節度使。

translations.literal: Critics did not cease; he was demoted to academician of the Hall of Asset Administration and magistrate of Yingchang Prefecture, transferred to Daming, and given the additional titles of academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and military commissioner of Fengguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: The critics did not cease. He was demoted to academician of the Hall of Asset Administration and magistrate of Yingchang Prefecture, transferred to Daming, and given the additional titles of academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and military commissioner of the Fengguo Army.

sentences.zh: 在大名六年，數告老，召為佑神觀使。

translations.literal: At Daming for six years, he repeatedly requested retirement and was summoned as commissioner of the Youshen Observatory.
translations.idiomatic: After six years at Daming, he repeatedly requested retirement and was summoned to serve as commissioner of the Youshen Observatory.

sentences.zh: 政和初，卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenghe he died, aged seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhenghe era he died, at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 贈開府儀同三司，諡曰「文定」。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies, with posthumous title "Wending" (Literary and Settled).
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given the title of Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies, with the posthumous name Wending, Literary and Settled.

sentences.zh: 子份，龍圖閣學士。

translations.literal: His son Fen was an academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fen became an academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall.

sentences.zh: 鄧潤甫

translations.literal: Deng Runfu
translations.idiomatic: Deng Runfu

sentences.zh: 鄧潤甫，字溫伯，建昌人。

translations.literal: Deng Runfu, styled Wenbo, a native of Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Runfu, styled Wenbo, was a native of Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 嘗避高魯王諱，以字為名，別字聖求，後皆復之。

translations.literal: He once avoided the taboo name of Prince Gao of Lu, using his style as his given name and taking the additional style Shengqiu; later all were restored.
translations.idiomatic: He once avoided the taboo name of Prince Gao of Lu, using his style as his given name and taking the additional style Shengqiu; later all were restored.

sentences.zh: 第進士，為上饒尉、武昌令。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and served as sheriff of Shangrao and magistrate of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and served as sheriff of Shangrao and magistrate of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 舉賢良方正，召試不應。

translations.literal: He was recommended as worthy and upright; summoned for examination he did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: He was recommended as worthy and upright, but when summoned for examination he did not respond.

sentences.zh: 熙寧中，王安石以潤甫為編修中書條例、檢正中書戶房事。

translations.literal: During Xining, Wang Anshi appointed Runfu to compile regulations of the Secretariat and to inspect and rectify the Secretariat's household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xining era, Wang Anshi appointed Runfu to compile regulations of the Secretariat and to inspect and rectify the Secretariat's household affairs.

sentences.zh: 神宗覽其文，除集賢校理、直舍人院，改知諫院、知制誥。

translations.literal: Shenzong read his writings and appointed him collator at the Hall of Assembled Worthies and duty in the Academy of Scholars, then changed him to director of the Remonstrance Bureau and drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong read his writings and appointed him collator at the Hall of Assembled Worthies with duty in the Academy of Scholars, then changed him to director of the Remonstrance Bureau and drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 同鄧綰、張琥治鄭俠獄，深致其文，入馮京、王安國、丁諷、王堯臣罪。

translations.literal: Together with Deng Wan and Zhang Hu he handled the Zheng Xia case, deeply pursuing his writings, and implicated Feng Jing, Wang Anguo, Ding Feng, and Wang Yaochén in guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Deng Wan and Zhang Hu he handled the Zheng Xia case, deeply pursuing his writings and implicating Feng Jing, Wang Anguo, Ding Feng, and Wang Yaochén.

sentences.zh: 擢御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 上疏曰：「向者陛下登用雋賢，更易百度，士狃於見聞，蔽於俗學，競起而萃非之，故陛下排斥異論，以圖治功。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: "Previously Your Majesty elevated outstanding talent and changed a hundred measures; scholars clung to what they had seen and heard, were blinded by conventional learning, and rose together to gather and criticize; therefore Your Majesty excluded dissenting views to seek governing achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial saying, "Previously Your Majesty elevated outstanding talent and changed a hundred measures. Scholars clung to what they had seen and heard, were blinded by conventional learning, and rose together to criticize. Therefore Your Majesty excluded dissenting views to seek governing achievement.

sentences.zh: 然言責之路，反為壅抑；

translations.literal: Yet the path of remonstrance was instead blocked;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the path of remonstrance was instead blocked;

sentences.zh: 非徒抑之，又或疑之。

translations.literal: not only suppressed but sometimes also suspected.
translations.idiomatic: not only suppressed but sometimes also suspected.

sentences.zh: 論恤民力，則疑其違道干譽；

translations.literal: Discussing relief for the people's strength, then suspecting violation of the Way and seeking reputation;
translations.idiomatic: Discuss relief for the people's burdens, and it is suspected of violating the Way and seeking reputation;

sentences.zh: 論補法度，則疑其同乎流俗；

translations.literal: discussing supplementing laws and institutions, then suspecting conformity with vulgar custom;
translations.idiomatic: discuss supplementing laws and institutions, and it is suspected of conforming to vulgar custom;

sentences.zh: 論斥人物，則疑其訐以為直。

translations.literal: discussing denouncing persons, then suspecting exposure for the sake of uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: discuss denouncing persons, and it is suspected of exposing others merely to appear upright.

sentences.zh: 故敢言之氣日以折，而天下事變，有不得盡聞。

translations.literal: Therefore the spirit of daring to speak daily waned, and changes in affairs under heaven could not all be fully heard.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the spirit of daring to speak waned day by day, and changes in affairs under heaven could not all reach Your Majesty's ears.

sentences.zh: 曩變法之初，勢自當爾。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the reforms, the situation naturally had to be so.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the reforms, the situation naturally had to be so.

sentences.zh: 今法度已就緒，宜有以來天下論議。

translations.literal: Now laws and institutions are already in order; there should be means to draw discussion from all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Now laws and institutions are already in order. There should be means to draw discussion from all under heaven.

sentences.zh: 至於淫辭詖行，有挾而發，自當屏棄。

translations.literal: As for licentious words and slanderous conduct, those who launch them with ulterior motives should naturally be rejected.
translations.idiomatic: As for licentious words and slanderous conduct launched with ulterior motives, those should naturally be rejected.

sentences.zh: 如此，則善言不伏，而致大治也。」

translations.literal: In this way, good words would not be suppressed, and great order would be achieved."
translations.idiomatic: In this way, good words would not be suppressed, and great order would be achieved."

sentences.zh: 李憲措置熙河邊事，潤甫率其屬周尹、蔡承禧、彭汝礪上書切諫，其略云：「自唐開元以來，用楊思勖、魚朝恩、程元振、吐突承璀為將。

translations.literal: Li Xian managed frontier affairs in Xihe; Runfu led his subordinates Zhou Yin, Cai Chengxi, and Peng Ruli in submitting a stern memorial; the gist said: "Since the Kaiyuan era of Tang, Yang Sixu, Yu Chao'en, Cheng Yuanzhen, and Tuhu Chenghuan were used as generals.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian managed frontier affairs in Xihe. Runfu led his subordinates Zhou Yin, Cai Chengxi, and Peng Ruli in submitting a stern memorial. The gist said, "Since the Kaiyuan era of the Tang dynasty, Yang Sixu, Yu Chao'en, Cheng Yuanzhen, and Tuhu Chenghuan were used as generals.

sentences.zh: 有功，則負勢驕恣，陵轢公卿；

translations.literal: When they had merit, they relied on power and were arrogant and unrestrained, trampling on dukes and ministers;
translations.idiomatic: When they had merit, they relied on power and were arrogant and unrestrained, trampling on dukes and ministers;

sentences.zh: 無功，則挫損國威，為四國笑。

translations.literal: when they had no merit, they damaged national prestige and became the laughter of the four states.
translations.idiomatic: when they had no merit, they damaged national prestige and became the laughingstock of the four states.

sentences.zh: 今陛下使憲將兵，功之成否，非臣等所能預料。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty has Xian lead troops; whether success or failure, we your ministers cannot foretell.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty has Xian lead troops. Whether he succeeds or fails, we your ministers cannot foretell.

sentences.zh: 然以往事監之，其有害必矣。

translations.literal: Yet taking past events as a mirror, harm is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Yet taking past events as a mirror, harm is certain.

sentences.zh: 陛下仁聖神武，駕御豪傑，雖憲百輩，顧何能為，獨不長念卻慮，為萬世之計乎？

translations.literal: Your Majesty is benevolent, sage, divine, and martial, controlling heroes—though Xian were a hundred men, what could they do? Will you not long consider and reflect for the plan of ten thousand generations?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is benevolent, sage, divine, and martial, controlling heroes. Though Xian were a hundred men, what could they do? Will you not long consider and reflect for the plan of ten thousand generations?

sentences.zh: 豈可使國史所書，以中人將兵自陛下始？

translations.literal: How can we allow the national histories to record that eunuch generals began with Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: How can we allow the national histories to record that eunuch generals began with Your Majesty?

sentences.zh: 後世沿襲故跡，視以為常，進用其徒握兵柄，則天下之患，將有不可勝言者矣！」

translations.literal: Later generations following old tracks would regard it as normal; advancing and using their kind to grasp military power—then calamity under heaven would be beyond words!
translations.idiomatic: Later generations following old tracks would regard it as normal. If their kind were advanced to grasp military power, calamity under heaven would be beyond words!

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: [The emperor] did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not listen.

sentences.zh: 又言：「興利之臣，議前代帝王陵寢，許民請射耕墾，而司農可之。

translations.literal: He also said: "Profit-seeking officials proposed that former dynasties' imperial tombs be opened to allow the people to apply for hunting, farming, and reclamation, and the Minister of Revenue approved.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Profit-seeking officials proposed that former dynasties' imperial tombs be opened to allow the people to apply for hunting, farming, and reclamation, and the Minister of Revenue approved.

sentences.zh: 唐之諸陵，因此悉見芟劉，昭陵喬木，翦伐無遺。

translations.literal: All the tombs of Tang were thus mowed and cut; the tall trees of Zhaoling were felled without remainder.
translations.idiomatic: All the tombs of the Tang dynasty were thus mowed and cut down. The tall trees of Zhaoling were felled without remainder.

sentences.zh: 熙寧著令，本禁樵采，遇郊祀則敕吏致祭，德意可謂遠矣。

translations.literal: The Xining established order originally forbade cutting firewood; when suburban sacrifices occurred, officials were ordered to perform rites—the benevolent intent can be called far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: The Xining established order originally forbade cutting firewood and gathering. When suburban sacrifices occurred, officials were ordered to perform rites. The benevolent intent can be called far-reaching.

sentences.zh: 小人掊克，不顧大體。

translations.literal: Petty men extort and do not consider the larger body.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men extort without regard for the larger good.

sentences.zh: 願絀創議之人，而一切如令。」

translations.literal: I wish to demote those who originated the proposal, and have everything follow the established order.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to demote those who originated the proposal and have everything follow the established order.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The emperor] consented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 遷翰林學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 因論奏相州獄，為蔡確所陷，落職知撫州。

translations.literal: Because he discussed and memorialized on the Xiangzhou case, he was framed by Cai Que, demoted, and made magistrate of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because he discussed and memorialized on the Xiangzhou case, he was framed by Cai Que, demoted, and made magistrate of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 移杭州，以龍圖閣直學士知成都府。

translations.literal: Transferred to Hangzhou, then as direct academician at the Dragon Diagram Hall made magistrate of Chengdu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hangzhou, then appointed magistrate of Chengdu Prefecture as direct academician at the Dragon Diagram Hall.

sentences.zh: 召復翰林學士兼掌皇子閣箋記，一時制作，獨倚潤甫焉。

translations.literal: Summoned back as Hanlin academician and concurrently in charge of the princes' pavilion documents; for a time all compositions relied solely on Runfu.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned back as Hanlin academician and put in charge of the princes' pavilion documents. For a time all compositions relied solely on Runfu.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，惟潤甫在院，一夕草制二十有二。

translations.literal: When Zhezong ascended, Runfu alone was in the academy; in one night he drafted twenty-two edicts.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong ascended the throne, Runfu alone was in the academy. In one night he drafted twenty-two edicts.

sentences.zh: 進承旨，修撰《神宗實錄》。

translations.literal: He was promoted to chief academician and compiled the Veritable Records of Shenzong.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to chief academician and compiled the Veritable Records of Shenzong.

sentences.zh: 以母喪去，終制，為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He left on his mother's death; after the mourning period ended, he became Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He left office on his mother's death. After the mourning period ended, he became Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 梁燾論其草蔡確制，妄稱有定策功，乃以龍圖閣學士知亳州。

translations.literal: Liang Tao argued that in drafting Cai Que's edict he falsely claimed merit in settling the succession; he was then made academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and magistrate of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Tao argued that in drafting Cai Que's edict he falsely claimed merit in settling the succession. He was then made academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and magistrate of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 閱歲，復以承旨召。

translations.literal: After a year he was again summoned as chief academician.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was again summoned as chief academician.

sentences.zh: 數月，除端明殿學士、禮部尚書。

translations.literal: After several months he was appointed academician of the Hall of Clear Brightness and Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After several months he was appointed academician of the Hall of Clear Brightness and Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 請郡，得知蔡州，移永興軍。

translations.literal: He requested a prefecture and was made magistrate of Caizhou, then transferred to Yongxing Army.
translations.idiomatic: He requested a prefectural post and was made magistrate of Caizhou, then transferred to Yongxing Army.

sentences.zh: 元祐末，以兵部尚書召。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanyou he was summoned as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuanyou era he was summoned as Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，哲宗親政，潤甫首陳武王能廣文王之聲，成王能嗣文、武之道，以開紹述。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaosheng, when Zhezong personally took power, Runfu first stated that King Wu could extend King Wen's fame and King Cheng could inherit the Way of Wen and Wu, to open the succession of the past.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shaosheng era, when Zhezong personally took power, Runfu was the first to state that King Wu extended King Wen's fame and King Cheng inherited the Way of Wen and Wu, thereby opening the succession of the past.

sentences.zh: 遂拜尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 章惇議重謫呂大防、劉摯，潤甫不以為然，曰：「俟見上，當力爭。」

translations.literal: Zhang Dun proposed heavy demotion for Lü Dafang and Liu Zhi; Runfu did not agree, saying: "Wait until I see the emperor—I will argue forcefully."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun proposed heavy demotion for Lü Dafang and Liu Zhi. Runfu did not agree, saying, "Wait until I see the emperor—I will argue forcefully."

sentences.zh: 無何，暴卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: Before long he suddenly died, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he suddenly died, at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 輟視朝二日。

translations.literal: Court audience was suspended for two days.
translations.idiomatic: Court audience was suspended for two days.

sentences.zh: 以嘗掌均邸箋奏，優贈開府儀同三司，諡曰「安惠」。

translations.literal: Because he had once managed the Jun princes' pavilion memorials, he was generously posthumously given Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies, with posthumous title "Anhui" (Peaceful and Kind).
translations.idiomatic: Because he had once managed the Jun princes' pavilion memorials, he was generously posthumously given the title of Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies, with the posthumous name Anhui, Peaceful and Kind.

sentences.zh: 林希，字子中，福州人。

translations.literal: Lin Xi, styled Zizhong, a native of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Xi, styled Zizhong, was a native of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，調涇縣主簿，為館閣校勘、集賢校理。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, was assigned as registrar of Jing County, and served as collator in the academies and collator at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, was assigned as registrar of Jing County, and served as collator in the academies and collator at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 神宗朝，同知太常禮院。

translations.literal: During Shenzong's reign he was associate director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: During Shenzong's reign he served as associate director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 皇后父喪，太常議服淺素，希奏：「禮，后為父降服期。

translations.literal: When the empress's father died, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices debated wearing light plain mourning; Xi memorialized: "According to rites, the empress for her father wears reduced mourning for one year.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress's father died, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices debated wearing light plain mourning. Xi memorialized, "According to rites, the empress for her father wears reduced mourning for one year.

sentences.zh: 今服淺素，不經。」

translations.literal: Now wearing light plain is not according to the classics."
translations.idiomatic: Wearing light plain mourning now is not according to the classics."

sentences.zh: 及遣使高麗，希聞命，懼形於色，辭行。

translations.literal: When an envoy was sent to Goryeo, Xi heard the order, fear showed on his face, and he declined to go.
translations.idiomatic: When he was ordered to serve as envoy to Goryeo, Xi heard the command, fear showed on his face, and he declined to go.

sentences.zh: 神宗怒，責監杭州樓店務。

translations.literal: Shenzong was angry and punished him by supervising the Hangzhou building-shop office.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong was angry and punished him by assigning him to supervise the Hangzhou building-shop office.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，通判秀州，復知太常禮院，遷著作佐郎、禮部郎中。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was vice-prefect of Xiuzhou, again director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and promoted to assistant director of the Bureau of Compilation and director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was made vice-prefect of Xiuzhou, again served as director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and was promoted to assistant director of the Bureau of Compilation and director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 元豐六年，詔修《兩朝寶訓》，上之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanfeng he was ordered to compile the Precious Instructions of the Two Reigns and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Yuanfeng era he was ordered to compile the Precious Instructions of the Two Reigns and submitted it.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，歷秘書少監、起居舍人、起居郎，進中書舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou he successively served as vice-director of the Secretariat, recorder of conduct, and director of conduct, and was promoted to drafter of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yuanyou era he successively served as vice-director of the Secretariat, recorder of conduct, and director of conduct, and was promoted to drafter of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 言者疏其行誼浮偽，士論羞薄，不足以玷從列。

translations.literal: Critics memorialized that his conduct and righteousness were shallow and false; scholarly opinion was ashamed and scornful, holding him unworthy to stain the attendant ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Critics memorialized that his conduct and righteousness were shallow and false. Scholarly opinion was ashamed and scornful, holding him unworthy to stain the attendant ranks.

sentences.zh: 以集賢殿修撰知蘇州，更宣、湖、潤、杭、亳五州，加天章閣待制。

translations.literal: He was made compiler at the Hall of Assembled Worthies and magistrate of Suzhou, then transferred through five prefectures—Xuan, Hu, Run, Hang, and Bo—and given the additional title of academician awaiting orders at the Hall of Heavenly Patterns.
translations.idiomatic: He was made compiler at the Hall of Assembled Worthies and magistrate of Suzhou, then transferred through five prefectures—Xuan, Hu, Run, Hang, and Bo—and given the additional title of academician awaiting orders at the Hall of Heavenly Patterns.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，進寶文閣直學士、知成都府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaosheng he was promoted to direct academician at the Hall of Precious Culture and made magistrate of Chengdu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shaosheng era, he was promoted to direct academician at the Hall of Precious Culture and appointed magistrate of Chengdu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 道闕下，會哲宗親政，章惇用事，嘗曰：「元祐初，司馬光作相，用蘇軾掌制，所以能鼓動四方，安得斯人而用之。」

translations.literal: Passing below the palace gate, when Zhezong personally took power and Zhang Dun held sway, [Zhang Dun] once said: "At the beginning of Yuanyou, Sima Guang was chief councilor and used Su Shi to draft edicts—that is how he could stir the four directions. Where can we find such a man to use?"
translations.idiomatic: Passing below the palace gate, when Zhezong personally took power and Zhang Dun held sway, Zhang Dun once said, "At the beginning of the Yuanyou era, Sima Guang was chief councilor and used Su Shi to draft edicts—that is how he stirred the four directions. Where can we find such a man to use?"

sentences.zh: 或曰：「希可。」

translations.literal: Someone said: "Xi will do."
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "Xi will do."

sentences.zh: 惇欲使希典書命，逞毒於元祐諸臣，且許以為執政。

translations.literal: Zhang Dun wished to have Xi manage documents and edicts, vent poison on the Yuanyou officials, and moreover promised to make him chief administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun wished to have Xi manage documents and edicts, vent his venom on the Yuanyou officials, and moreover promised to make him chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 希亦以久不得志，將甘心焉，遂留行。

translations.literal: Xi also, having long failed to achieve his ambitions, was willing to submit to this, and so remained and proceeded.
translations.idiomatic: Xi also, having long failed to achieve his ambitions, was willing to submit to this, and so remained and proceeded.

sentences.zh: 復為中書舍人，修《神宗實錄》兼侍讀。

translations.literal: He again became drafter of the Secretariat, compiling the Veritable Records of Shenzong and concurrently serving as lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: He again became drafter of the Secretariat, compiling the Veritable Records of Shenzong while concurrently serving as lecturer.

sentences.zh: 哲宗問：「神宗殿曰『宣光』，前代有此名乎？」

translations.literal: Zhezong asked: "Shenzong's hall is called 'Xuanguang'—did former dynasties have this name?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhezong asked, "Shenzong's hall is called Xuanguang—did former dynasties have this name?"

sentences.zh: 希對曰：「此石勒殿名也。」

translations.literal: Xi replied: "This was the name of Shi Le's hall."
translations.idiomatic: Xi replied, "That was the name of Shi Le's hall."

sentences.zh: 乃更為「顯承」。

translations.literal: It was then changed to "Xiancheng."
translations.idiomatic: It was then changed to Xiancheng.

sentences.zh: 時方推明紹述，盡黜元祐群臣，希皆密豫其議。

translations.literal: At the time they were promoting the succession of the past and dismissing all Yuanyou ministers; Xi secretly participated in all these deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: At the time they were promoting the succession of the past and dismissing all Yuanyou ministers. Xi secretly participated in all these deliberations.

sentences.zh: 自司馬光、呂公著、大防、劉摯、蘇軾、轍等數十人之制，皆希為之，詞極其醜詆，至以「老奸擅國」之語陰斥宣仁，讀者無不憤歎。

translations.literal: From the edicts for Sima Guang, Lü Gongzhu, Dafang, Liu Zhi, Su Shi, Zhe, and dozens of others—all were drafted by Xi; the language was extremely ugly and slanderous, even using the phrase "old traitor monopolizing the state" to secretly denounce Xuanren; readers were all indignant and sighing.
translations.idiomatic: The edicts for Sima Guang, Lü Gongzhu, Dafang, Liu Zhi, Su Shi, Zhe, and dozens of others were all drafted by Xi. The language was extremely ugly and slanderous, even using the phrase "old traitor monopolizing the state" to secretly denounce Empress Xuanren. Readers were all indignant and sighing.

sentences.zh: 一日，希草制罷，擲筆於 地曰：「壞了名節矣。」

translations.literal: One day, when Xi finished drafting an edict, he threw the brush to the ground and said: "I have ruined my reputation and integrity."
translations.idiomatic: One day, when Xi finished drafting an edict, he threw the brush to the ground and said, "I have ruined my reputation and integrity."

sentences.zh: 遷禮部，吏部尚書、翰林學士，擢同知樞密院。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of Rites, then Minister of Personnel and Hanlin academician, and promoted to associate director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Ministry of Rites, then served as Minister of Personnel and Hanlin academician, and was promoted to associate director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 始，惇疑曾布在樞府間己，使希為貳，以相伺察。

translations.literal: At first Zhang Dun suspected Zeng Bu in the Bureau of Military Affairs was undermining him, and made Xi second-in-command to watch and investigate each other.
translations.idiomatic: At first Zhang Dun suspected Zeng Bu in the Bureau of Military Affairs was undermining him, and made Xi second-in-command so the two could watch and investigate each other.

sentences.zh: 希日為布所誘，且怨惇不引為執政，遂叛惇。

translations.literal: Xi daily was enticed by Bu, and also resented Zhang Dun for not recommending him as chief administrator, and so turned against Zhang Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was daily enticed by Bu, and also resented Zhang Dun for not recommending him as chief administrator, and so turned against Zhang Dun.

sentences.zh: 會邢恕論希罪，惇因並去之，罷知亳州，移杭州，布不能救也。

translations.literal: When Xing Shu discussed Xi's crimes, Zhang Dun took the opportunity to remove them both; Xi was dismissed to be magistrate of Bozhou, transferred to Hangzhou, and Bu could not save him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xing Shu discussed Xi's crimes, Zhang Dun took the opportunity to remove them both. Xi was dismissed to serve as magistrate of Bozhou, then transferred to Hangzhou, and Bu could not save him.

sentences.zh: 旋以端明殿學士知太原府。

translations.literal: Shortly he was made academician of the Hall of Clear Brightness and magistrate of Taiyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was made academician of the Hall of Clear Brightness and magistrate of Taiyuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，徙大名。

translations.literal: When Huizong ascended, he was transferred to Daming.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong ascended the throne, he was transferred to Daming.

sentences.zh: 上河東邊計三策，朝廷以其詞命醜正之罪，奪職知揚州，徙舒州。

translations.literal: He submitted three plans for the Hedong frontier; the court, taking his language as the crime of maligning the upright, stripped his office and made him magistrate of Yangzhou, then transferred him to Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted three plans for the Hedong frontier. The court, taking his language as the crime of maligning the upright, stripped his office and made him magistrate of Yangzhou, then transferred him to Shuzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒，年六十七。

translations.literal: Before long he died, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died, at the age of sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 追贈資政殿學士，諡曰「文節」。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given academician of the Hall of Asset Administration, with posthumous title "Wenjie" (Literary and Principled).
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given the title of academician of the Hall of Asset Administration, with the posthumous name Wenjie, Literary and Principled.

sentences.zh: 弟旦。

translations.literal: His younger brother Dan.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Dan.

sentences.zh: 弟 旦

translations.literal: Younger brother Dan
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Dan

sentences.zh: 旦，第進士，熙寧中，由著作佐郎主管淮南常平，擢太子中允、監察御史裏行。

translations.literal: Dan passed the jinshi examination; during Xining, from assistant director of the Bureau of Compilation he supervised Huainan Ever-Normal Granaries, and was promoted to palace attendant and acting censor.
translations.idiomatic: Dan passed the jinshi examination. During the Xining era, from assistant director of the Bureau of Compilation he supervised Huainan Ever-Normal Granaries, and was promoted to palace attendant and acting censor.

sentences.zh: 居臺五月，以論李定事罷守故官。

translations.literal: After five months at the Censorate, he was dismissed for discussing the Li Ding affair and returned to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: After five months at the Censorate, he was dismissed for discussing the Li Ding affair and returned to his former post.

sentences.zh: 久之，幹當奏院；

translations.literal: After a long time he managed the Memorials Office;
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was assigned to manage the Memorials Office;

sentences.zh: 陳繹領門下封駁，又摭其前論罷之。

translations.literal: Chen Yi led the Chancellery's review and rejection, and again seized on his earlier discussion to dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yi led the Chancellery's review and rejection section, and again seized on his earlier discussion to dismiss him.

sentences.zh: 累年，乃簽書淮南判官。

translations.literal: After several years he became signing secretary and judge of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he became signing secretary and judge of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 入為太常博士，工部、考功員外郎。

translations.literal: He entered [the capital] as doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and vice-director in the Ministries of Works and Merit.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and vice-director in the Ministries of Works and Merit.

sentences.zh: 元祐元年，拜殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanyou he was appointed palace censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yuanyou era he was appointed palace censor.

sentences.zh: 甫蒞職，即上疏曰：「廣言路然後知得失，達民情然後知利病。

translations.literal: As soon as he took office, he submitted a memorial saying: "Broaden the path of speech and then one knows gain and loss; reach the people's sentiments and then one knows benefit and harm.
